channel.title: AV Pain Reliever
channel.description: AV Pain Reliever — release feed for the Sparkle auto-updater.

item.title: Version 0.1.11
item.description:
What's new

  • The update window now comes to the front when you click Check for Updates instead of hiding behind your other apps.
  • The update window has a proper "Software Update" title and a What's New panel sourced from each release.

item.title: Version 0.1.12
item.description:
What's new

Listen, the old icon was two pills, playing it cute. The new icon is one refined capsule on a charcoal squircle — same brand wink, way more "I'm a serious utility." Big improvement, just look at it.

Also — and this is the real one — there's a Menu bar icon picker now. Settings → General. Eighteen SF symbols to choose from. Mic, camera, sliders, waveforms, switching arrows, the works. We even snuck a party popper in there, because why not — the About window already throws confetti, we're keeping the bit going.

Quick technical thing: the picker turns off when the per-profile icon setting is on. The active profile's icon is already doing the work; don't want two settings tripping over each other — that's amateur hour. The caption tells you exactly what's happening.

That's the update. New icon, new picker, eighteen options. Money.

item.title: Version 0.1.13
item.description:
What's new

Listen, the switch notification — the little banner that pops up when you change docks — used to show our app icon. Just the app icon. Every time. Fine, but generic. We're upgrading. Now the notification shows the active profile's icon: house for home office, laptop for laptop, whatever you set. Per-profile. Per-switch. Sharp.

The "new location detected" notification gets the question-mark glyph too, same one the menu bar shows. Consistent system, top to bottom.

That's the deal. New thumbnail on the toast. Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0
item.description:
What's new

OK here's the deal. v0.2.0 is the big one. AV Pain Reliever is now a virtual camera. That's right — the same app that's been quietly swapping your audio defaults all this time can now also be the camera that Zoom, Slack, Teams, and any other video app picks up. One camera in their picker. One name. AV Pain Reliever. It streams whatever real camera the active profile names — your built-in webcam at the laptop, the HDMI capture at the home office, your iPhone via Continuity at the conference room — whatever you've configured. The profile changes, the picture follows. Money.

Here's what this fixes: Zoom, Slack, and Teams keep their own camera selection that ignores the system default. So back in v0.1.x when you docked at a new location, your microphone and speakers would change, but Zoom would just sit there showing your laptop webcam like nothing happened. That's amateur hour. With v0.2.0, you pick "AV Pain Reliever" in Zoom once and you're done. Forever.

It's off by default — installing a virtual camera is a real thing and we're not turning it on without your permission, that's not how we do business. Open Settings → Camera and flip the toggle. macOS will ask you to approve the extension once (System Settings → Login Items & Extensions → Camera Extensions). After that, you're in.

A few technical things, briefly, because if you're reading this far you probably care:

  • Hold-last-frame during the swap. When you change profiles, the new camera takes a beat to warm up — about half a second. Instead of flashing black at your Zoom call, the virtual camera holds the last frame from the old camera until the new one's delivering frames. You see a soft pause; nobody on the call sees a glitch.
  • Format conversion for any camera. Built-in webcams ship BGRA, USB capture cards ship YUV at 1080p, every device has its quirks. We accept whatever the camera natively delivers and convert to 1280×720 BGRA on the fly, hardware-accelerated where possible. Means your weird HDMI capture card just works.
  • Profile-driven everywhere. The same Add Profile wizard that picks your audio defaults now also picks the camera the virtual camera streams. No new config to learn — it's the same camera field you've already been using. v0.1.x configs upgrade clean.

One known thing: if you toggle the virtual camera off and then back on inside the same launch, macOS holds the extension in a stale state and the feed goes black. The Settings UI catches this and gives you a Restart AV Pain Reliever button that handles it. One click, fresh process, you're back. Edge case — most folks turn it on once and leave it. Not a deal-breaker.

That's the update. Virtual camera, profile-driven, hold-last-frame, universal format support. v0.1.x will keep getting patch releases in parallel for anyone who doesn't need any of this. Money.

item.title: Version 0.1.14
item.description:
What's new

Listen, here's the deal. v0.2.0 shipped yesterday with the virtual camera — Zoom, Slack, Teams, the whole crew finally following your profile. Big release. But here's the thing: a virtual camera is a system extension, which means macOS asks for approval, the in-Settings toggle has a known quirk, and frankly we're not ready to push that on every user as the default upgrade. That's not how we do business.

So v0.1.14 brings you a switch. Settings → General → Updates → "Receive experimental updates." Off by default — you keep getting the steady stream of v0.1.x patches like nothing happened. Flip it on, and you're now on the early-access track: v0.2.0's virtual camera shows up as your next upgrade, you go through the system-extension dance, you're streaming whatever camera the active profile names into Zoom. Money. Flip it back off, you're back on the stable line. No commitments. Pick your speed.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.1
item.description:
What's new

Quick patch. v0.1.14 just shipped the "Receive experimental updates" toggle that lets v0.1.x users opt into v0.2.x — but if you're already on v0.2.0, you didn't have that toggle yet. Catch-22. v0.2.0.1 fixes it: Settings → General → Updates now has the same toggle you saw in v0.1.14, defaulting off. Flip it on if you want future v0.2.x patches to roll in automatically; leave it off and you stay on v0.2.0.1 until something stable enough hits the main line. Pick your speed. Money.

item.title: Version 0.1.15
item.description:
What's new

Quick fix. Some USB capture cards — looking at you, the cheap HDMI-to-USB ones — expose their serial number through one IOKit key but not the other. AV Pain Reliever was only checking one of those keys, so if your profile fingerprint pinned a specific serial for a card like that, we'd silently miss the match and fall back to your laptop profile every time. Worked great for everything except the cards that mattered. Patched. Now we check both keys, the serial comes through, your fingerprint matches when you dock, the right profile applies. Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.2
item.description:
What's new

Same fix as v0.1.15 — that USB serial-number gotcha where some capture cards only expose one of the two IOKit keys (the raw kUSBSerialNumberString instead of the friendly "USB Serial Number"). Now we read both. If your dock has one of those quirky cards in the fingerprint and the engine was mysteriously falling back to your laptop profile every relaunch, this is the fix. Dock, launch, the right profile applies. Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.3
item.description:
What's new

UX cleanup. Before this, if you were running the experimental v0.2.x with the "Receive experimental updates" toggle off, clicking Check for Updates would tell you "you're up to date" and report v0.1.15 as the newest available — even though you're running v0.2.0, which is higher. Confusing. Technically Sparkle was filtering the appcast to stable-only because no channels were allowlisted, but nobody reads it that way.

Now the dialog explains the actual situation. Click Check for Updates on an experimental build with the toggle off, you get a tailored alert with three buttons: Enable Experimental Updates (flips the switch and runs the check fresh, this time seeing experimental items), Check Stable Anyway (the old behavior, for the rare case you want to confirm what stable says), or Cancel. One click to actually be on the experimental track instead of squinting at a contradictory dialog. Money.

item.title: Version 0.1.16
item.description:
What's new

Wizard refinements. Two of them, one release.

The device list in Add Profile is sorted properly now. Location-defining gear — mics, speakers, cameras, capture cards, your dock, displays — floats to the top. Travel peripherals — keyboards, mice, phones, AirPods — sink to the bottom with their existing Suggested: untick pill. No more squinting past Apple Magic Keyboard to find Yeti Stereo Microphone.

Also: if you untick every device in the list, the wizard now tells you what that means. Zero devices = fallback profile = matches whenever no other profile does (typically your laptop, undocked). Before, it just showed the generic "uncheck the peripherals" caption regardless of state. Now it flips to a labeled hint the second you clear the selection — so if you didn't mean to ship a fallback, the wizard catches you. Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.4
item.description:
What's new

Brings the wizard refinements from v0.1.16 over to the experimental track. Two improvements you'll feel the next time you click Add Profile:

The device list is sorted properly now. Mics, speakers, cameras, capture cards, your dock, displays — anything that defines a location — float to the top. Travel peripherals (keyboards, mice, phones, AirPods) sink to the bottom with their existing Suggested: untick pill. The hardware that defines your dock is right where you'd look first.

And if you untick everything in the list, the wizard now tells you what that means: zero devices = fallback profile, matches whenever no other profile does (typically your laptop, undocked). The caption flips to a labeled hint the second you clear the selection — so if you didn't mean to ship a fallback, you'll catch it before saving. Money.

item.title: Version 0.1.17
item.description:
What's new

Two more wizard polish items, both shaken loose by real-world testing on the docked-mac.

The device list sort actually does what the v0.1.16 release notes said it does now. Turns out the previous tiering was only catching the bottom — keyboards, mice, phones — leaving everything else jumbled in alphabetical order. Mics and audio interfaces would just sit wherever the alphabet put them. Fixed: there's now a positive priority tier at the top for anything with "microphone", "audio", "speaker", "camera", "capture", or "display" in its name. Three real tiers — priority, neutral, portable — with alphabetical within each. So Blue Microphones and CalDigit Thunderbolt 3 Audio finally land where they belong: top of the list, where you can see them.

Also: the wizard has been quietly auto-filling profile names from your dock signature for a while now (CalDigit detected → "Home Office", Yeti detected → "Studio", and so on). Behaviorally helpful, visually mysterious — looks like the wizard read your mind. Now the slug-preview caption prefixes with a bolded "Suggested." when the name came from auto-fill. Edit the name to anything and the prefix drops. So you know what the wizard did, and you know it's a guess you can override. Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.5
item.description:
What's new

Brings the v0.1.17 wizard polish over to the experimental track. Two improvements you'll see the next time you click Add Profile:

The device list sort actually does what the v0.2.0.4 release notes said it does. Previously the tier logic was only catching keyboards and mice at the bottom — leaving mics and audio interfaces in alphabetical position with everything else. Now there's a real priority tier at the top: anything with "microphone", "audio", "speaker", "camera", "capture", or "display" in the name floats up. Three tiers (priority → neutral → portable), alphabetical within each. Blue Microphones and CalDigit Thunderbolt 3 Audio land where they belong.

Also: the wizard's quiet auto-fill of profile names from your dock signature is now visible. CalDigit attached → "Home Office" used to just appear in the field. Now the slug-preview caption prefixes with a bolded "Suggested." when the value came from auto-fill, and the prefix drops the moment you edit the name. Less mysterious, same labor savings. Money.

item.title: Version 0.1.18
item.description:
What's new

The Add Profile wizard got smart enough to do most of the work for you. Three coordinated upgrades, all in one release.

The wizard used to start with every USB device on your dock pre-ticked — your microphone, your dock, your monitor, your keyboard, your trackpad, your phone, all checked. Your job was to scan the list and untick the stuff that travels with you. Easy to forget, easy to wind up with a Magic Keyboard quietly hardcoded into your home-office fingerprint. Now it flips: AV Pain Reliever pre-ticks only the headline hardware (microphones, cameras, capture cards, dedicated audio interfaces — the stuff that genuinely defines a location) and leaves everything else unticked. You actively tick what else matters. Cleaner fingerprints, less squinting.

To make the new defaults legible at a glance, every row in the device list now wears one of three states. Green "Important: " pill on the auto-ticked headline gear (Important: microphone, Important: capture card, Important: audio interface). Muted gray "Travels with you" pill on portable peripherals — keyboards, mice, phones, AirPods, watches — auto-unticked, the pill explains why your iPhone is in the list but not selected. No pill on neutral things like hub legs, displays, card readers, Stream Decks — quietly available, tick if you want them in your fingerprint. The old yellow "Suggested: untick" nudge is gone — once the suggestion is the default, the nudge is redundant.

Also: the wizard's profile-name auto-suggest finally checks if you already have a profile by that name. CalDigit dock attached used to silently fill in "Home Office" even if you already had a Home Office profile, queueing up a save-time collision dialog you had to fight through. Now it suppresses the suggestion and leaves the field empty — because if you're hitting Add Profile, you want a new profile, and pre-loading a name you already use is just signing you up for an argument with the wizard. Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.6
item.description:
What's new

Brings the v0.1.18 wizard rework over to the experimental track.

The Add Profile wizard used to start with every USB device pre-ticked and ask you to scan for the ones to remove. Now it flips: only the headline hardware (microphones, cameras, capture cards, dedicated audio interfaces) is auto-ticked. Everything else is visible but unticked — you actively tick anything else that defines this location.

To make it legible, every device row wears one of three states. Green "Important: " on the auto-ticked headline gear. Muted gray "Travels with you" on portable peripherals (keyboards, mice, phones) — auto-unticked, the pill explains why your iPhone is in the list but not selected. No pill on neutral things like hub legs, displays, card readers — quietly available. The old yellow "Suggested: untick" nudge retired; once unticked is the default, the nudge is just noise.

Plus: the wizard's profile-name auto-suggest finally checks for collisions. CalDigit attached used to silently fill in "Home Office" even when you already had one. Now it suppresses the suggestion if the slug is already in your config — leaving the field empty so you actually name your new profile. Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.7
item.description:
What's new

Two big quality-of-life wins on the virtual camera.

The green camera light used to stay on the whole time the app was open. Just… lit. Like someone was watching. Not anymore — capture only fires up when something's actually reading the virtual camera. Zoom call ends? Light's off in 30 seconds. Idle for an hour? Light's been off for fifty-nine and a half. The way it should be.

The other thing: the profile camera picker no longer lets you pick "AV Pain Reliever" from the list. Why would you? It's the OUTPUT. The thing Zoom is pointed at. Your profile names the REAL camera — the BRIO, the FaceTime HD, the capture card — and AV Pain Reliever routes it through. Plus, when the virtual camera is on, macOS's system camera preference now also points at AV Pain Reliever, so FaceTime and Safari follow the same routing as Zoom. One source of truth. Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.8
item.description:
What's new

Conference room save. The Neat Bar at the office was making the virtual camera freeze on one frame — sometimes, when you opened Zoom AFTER docking. Behind the scenes, the host was opening AV Pain Reliever as its OWN source. Self-source. Feedback loop. The frame you saw was just the same cached image echoing through the loop forever. Not great.

Two fixes. The host now refuses to ever open the virtual camera as a source — that's its own output, would be like recording yourself recording yourself. And when a profile says "use the Neat Bar" but Zoom isn't open yet, we hold onto that — so when Zoom DOES connect, the host opens the Neat Bar on the first try. Not the virtual camera. Not whatever the system thinks is preferred. The right camera. First try. Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.9
item.description:
What's new

Three things in one drop.

A new Stats tab in Settings. Opt-in, off by default — you flip the switch when you want it on. After that, every profile switch, manual override, streak day, and unique USB device gets counted locally. No content, no telemetry, no phoning home. Just numbers about your setup, on your Mac. The "Most-used location" line is the one that hits.

The Add and Edit Profile windows finally match Settings visually. They were lined up wrong — gray cards in the wizard pushed against the window edges while Settings had breathing room. Took a few iterations to nail. Now they're family.

Cleaner pills in the wizard's USB list. "mic" instead of "microphone." "video" covers cameras AND HDMI capture cards (capture cards aren't really cameras but they're video sources from your point of view — one word covers it). "audio" for the catch-all. And the list itself sorts smart: important stuff at the top, the "(unnamed device)" entries (those internal hub-leg things you never tick) pushed to the bottom. Easier to scan in two seconds. Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.10
item.description:
What's new

Polish drop. No new features — pure surface work. The kind of release where you open Settings, look around, and your shoulders drop a quarter-inch.

The wizard footer. Cancel used to be a button-with-an-X, Save was a button-with-a-plus. Apple's Cancel buttons have never had icons, never will. Ours shouldn't either. Fixed. Both are clean text now, the way every native sheet on macOS is.

The Profiles tab. The "Add Profile" button at the bottom isn't a big blue chunk anymore — it's a quiet bordered "Add Profile…" with an ellipsis, the way System Settings actually does it. The pencil and trash on each profile row lost their bordered chips. Just icons, no chrome, rows can breathe. Looks like Mail. Looks like Reminders.

The "Restart required" state on the Camera tab used to put a tiny grey button next to a big orange dot — the dot yelling, the button whispering. Now they match. And the Reset stats button on the Stats tab is finally a full-width red row inside its grouped section, the way Apple ID does Sign Out. Red text, full row, no ambiguity about which button is the dangerous one.

Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.11
item.description:
What's new

Polish drop. One fix, but it's been quietly bugging us for months.

The bottom of the Profiles tab. That strip with the Add Profile button and the "4 profiles" count? It's been a faux bottom bar all this time — a custom HStack with a Divider above it, dressed up to LOOK like a native Mac bar but never actually being one. The button inside always read a little off, a little flat, a little not-quite-Apple. Could never quite put a finger on why.

Fixed. It's a real macOS bottom bar now — translucent material chrome, automatic separator, the same kind of bar Mail uses under the mailbox sidebar and Reminders uses under the lists. And the Add Profile affordance is now the universal Apple + icon at bottom-left, the way Mail does new mailboxes, Reminders does new lists, and System Settings → Network does interface +/-. Hover it for the tooltip. Borderless, minimal, instantly recognizable.

Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.12
item.description:
What's new

Rendering fix. Buttons throughout the app got slightly cleaner — flatter, more native. Same intent, more polish.

What actually happened: every release until this one got compiled on GitHub's CI with an older Xcode that drew SwiftUI buttons one way; the dev's Mac has a newer Xcode that drew them the other way. The dev kept seeing the new look on his screen and accidentally shipping the old look to everyone else. Same source code, two different runtime paths into SwiftUI. Apple keeps both alive forever for backward compatibility, so the SDK at compile time picks which one your binary calls.

Now the build pipeline runs on the dev's actual Mac, with the actual Xcode he develops with. What lands in your /Applications is now the same look he sees on his own screen. Same toolchain, same SwiftUI runtime path, every time.

Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.13
item.description:
What's new

Polish drop — three separate UI wins on one release.

Profiles tab got a real makeover. That row of devices per profile used to be a single inline blob — icon, name, bullet, icon, name, bullet — that wrapped however it felt like, sometimes splitting a microphone icon from its label across two lines. Now each device gets its own row, icons aligned in a column on the left, mic and speaker and camera and connected-stuff stacked clean. Reads like a real Mac app instead of a wall of text with icon islands.

Native alerts everywhere. The "Delete profile?" confirmation used to render with the app's pill icon stamped in the corner — old AppKit pattern, doesn't match the rest of the system. Gone. Now it's the same flat sheet you see for "Reset stats?" and every other macOS confirmation. And there's a new "Turn off the virtual camera?" prompt that pops up before you accidentally disable Zoom and Slack and Teams' source of truth. Cancel snaps the toggle right back without ever entering the broken half-state macOS gets into when you toggle the camera extension off in the same session.

The USB icon swap. The old cable.connector glyph reads as a stick figure at small sizes — really, look at it next to a microphone glyph, it's a guy. Replaced everywhere with externaldrive.connected.to.line.below, which is unambiguously "thing plugged into your computer." Plus a copy pass that drops the app from naming itself in places where it was talking to itself in the third person. Cleaner everywhere.

Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.14
item.description:
What's new

About-window polish.

The version line under the big bold app name used to repeat the app name AND show the build number twice — "AV Pain Reliever 0.2.0.13 (0.2.0.13)", like the dialog wasn't sure you'd believe what app you were looking at. Cleaned up. Now it just says "Version 0.2.0.13", same as Apple's own About panel. One line, one piece of information.

There's also a new fortune slip floating in the middle of the About window. Cream-colored paper, italic serif text, slight tilt, soft drop shadow — looks like the slip you'd find inside a fortune cookie. Inside, one of fifty oracular pronouncements from a brilliant oracle who has nothing to do with audio or cameras and just wants to tell you something true about being a person. "What you have configured will configure you back." That one. Or one of forty-nine others. Different each time you open the window.

Plus a small copyright line at the bottom with a link to the source on GitHub for the truly curious.

Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.15
item.description:
OK here's the deal. v0.2.0.15 is mostly a face-lift. New app icon. Out goes the gray squircle with the floating pill capsule; in comes a pale icy-blue squircle with a single clean USB-fingerprint glyph in Apple-system-blue. It's the same symbol the wizard uses when you set up a location, so Dock, menu bar, and the in-app vocabulary now all match. Looks at home next to Calculator, Reminders, and the rest of the modern Mac icon family. Sharp on white wallpapers, doesn't dissolve, single defined edge. Money.

The menu bar default updates to the same glyph. If you'd customized your menu bar pick, you keep your pick. If you were on the original pill default, you'll see the new one show up after this update. Don't worry about it. Your pill is still in the picker (Settings → Behavior → Menu bar icon) if you miss it. The party-popper is still in there too.

A few small ones while we're here:

  • Camera permission prompt got tightened up. It used to say "AV Pain Reliever" three times in one dialog. We get it. We're AV Pain Reliever. Cleaner copy, same meaning.
  • About window: title is just "About" now (the rest of the window already says the app's name, no need to double up), the fortune-slip drifts toward the middle, and the Check for Updates button has room to breathe.
  • Settings opens on General every time, like Apple's own Settings does. No more landing on Stats because that's where you happened to be last week.

That's the whole thing. Update, enjoy the new icon, get back to work. You're gonna love it.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.16
item.description:
Alright, you're gonna like this one. v0.2.0.16 is a stability + diagnostics release. The headliner: the camera-extension visibility race is fixed. Once in a while at a fresh launch with the virtual camera enabled, the host process couldn't see its own newly-activated extension fast enough, and the app would surface a "Restart AV Pain Reliever" button at you like it'd given up. Three follow-on fixes, the race is closed, and the Restart button goes back to being the last-resort it was always meant to be.

A few more in there:

  • New menu item: Advanced → Save Logs for Support… Click it, pick a spot, the app dumps the last hour of unified-log entries to a plain text file you can email when something's off. There's also a new verbose .debug channel under the hood (silent by default, always available via log stream --level debug). Lets us actually debug a problem from a real machine without bolting on telemetry.

  • Stats tab gets per-profile rankings. A real ranked list of the locations you've spent your time at. Plus a fix you'd never notice unless you noticed: deleting a profile now actually clears its stats too. No more ghost rankings hanging out.

  • Cancel actually means cancel. Toggle the virtual camera off, click Cancel on the macOS admin-password prompt, and the app stays running like nothing happened. No more bouncing into a "failed" state and forcing a restart you didn't want. Small thing. Felt great to fix.

  • Wizard cleanups. Save a new profile and the engine auto-switches to it. The name field gets focus every time you open Add Profile. Edit-rename collisions spell out what's about to get deleted in plain English, not cryptic referee-speak.

  • Behind the scenes. Two-pass code-quality review of the engine and the app target shipped. Dead helpers gone. Near-duplicate views consolidated. Doc comments pointing at functions that don't exist anymore — gone. You won't notice unless you're reading the code; if you are, hi, the codebase is tighter.

That's the whole thing. Auto-update grabs it on the next check. Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.17-dev.1
item.description:
Alright. First dev release. Money.

You're at home. Conference Room dock is at the conference room. You want to swap Conference Room's mic from the Yeti to an AT2020. Tough luck, pal. The Yeti's not plugged in, you don't see it in the dropdown, you're stuck waiting for next Tuesday. Or you were. This is the edit-from-anywhere release.

What's new:

  • The wizard remembers your devices. Open Edit on any profile from anywhere and its saved audio + camera selections show up, marked "(not connected)" if they're not currently attached. Swap them, change your mind, pick something else. The cache is per-profile so your Home Office CalDigit doesn't leak into Conference Room's mic dropdown. That'd be amateur hour.

  • Soft warning when two profiles share a fingerprint. Two profiles claiming the same dock means only one of them ever auto-applies. The wizard now catches it at save time. Save Anyway, Cancel, you pick. Money.

  • Profiles sort alphabetically. Home Office, Laptop, Studio. Every launch. Stable order in the menu bar and in Settings → Profiles. Used to be hash-randomized between sessions which was, in technical terms, just nuts.

  • Edit-mode list puts your saved fingerprint at the top. Even if half the devices aren't plugged in. You see what this profile IS, not what happens to be plugged in right now. Big difference when you're editing from somewhere else.

  • Pills cleaned up. "Not connected", "Travels with you", "Important: Mic / Video / Audio / Speaker", "In Home Office" (when you're looking at a device that belongs to another profile). Sentence case across the board. The kind of detail you don't notice until you do.

  • Forget unused devices lives in Settings → General. One-click cleanup that trims each profile's remembered list to only what it actually uses. For when one-off coffee shop visits clutter things up.

Hey: it's the first dev release. First time we've shipped to the dev channel. If you're reading this in the app, you opted in via Settings → General → "Receive dev updates" — welcome aboard. Same builds, slightly faster cadence, smaller batches of in-flight features. Stuff that doesn't necessarily need to wait for a stable cut.

If you hit anything weird, file an issue or hit Save Logs for Support under the Advanced menu. Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.17-dev.2
item.description:
Here's a small one, dev.2. The config file you've been hand-editing? You're done clicking Reload. Save it. Reload happens. Money.

What's new:

  • Auto-reload on file edit. Hand-edit ~/Library/Application Support/AVPainReliever/profiles.toml in any text editor (TextEdit, VS Code, vim, doesn't matter, doesn't care). Save the file, the engine reloads within a quarter second. Audio defaults switch, camera switches, notification pops if the active profile changed. You stay in your editor.

  • Two buttons retired from Advanced. "Re-evaluate Now" and "Reload Config" are gone. The first was a legacy diagnostic that didn't really do anything you couldn't get from looking at the menu bar pill. The second is now redundant — the auto-reload watcher does the same job continuously, no click required. Same capability, cleaner submenu.

Under the hood there are two kqueue sources running together. One watches the parent directory for atomic-rename saves. The other watches the file inode for in-place saves. Whichever way your editor commits the bytes, we catch it. Belt-and-suspenders rebind handles the rare multi-step save dance. And there's a small mtime gate so the wizard's force-apply doesn't get undone by the watcher's 250 ms-later callback. Subtle, load-bearing.

Hit anything weird, save logs under Advanced → Save Logs for Support. Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.17-dev.3
item.description:
Quick one, dev.3. If you hand-edit profiles.toml and save a typo, the app no longer eats your config. Money.

Here's what was happening: parse error in profiles.toml meant the app wrote the default starter file right over the top of yours. Custom profiles, fingerprints, audio + camera selections — every one of them, gone. Silently. Auto-reload made that catastrophically easy: one bad save, 250 ms later, gone. Not how we do business.

Now when the parser chokes:

  • Your broken file gets renamed to profiles.corrupted-{timestamp}.toml right next to the active config. Same folder, different name, you can fix it and copy the sections back at your leisure.
  • A notification fires titled "Couldn't read profiles.toml" with a Show in Finder button that opens the Application Support folder with your broken file selected. One click, you're staring at the data you almost lost.
  • The freshly-installed starter takes over so the engine has something to apply while you sort it out. Once you fix the TOML and save, auto-reload picks it up like nothing happened.

If the rename itself fails (read-only volume, permissions weirdness), the app leaves your broken file alone and tells you to grab logs via Advanced → Save Logs for Support. Strictly better than the old behavior, which was to overwrite anyway. Money.

Hit anything weird, that same Save Logs button is your friend.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.17-dev.4
item.description:
Tiny one, dev.4. Nothing you'll notice. Behind the scenes, the file watcher now leaves a paper trail: started here, saw a save there, file inode changed (old to new), debounce armed, all that. Internal-only, no user-visible behavior changes. Money.

Why bother shipping it: when somebody files a "I saved my profile file and nothing happened" report, the saved support log finally has enough breadcrumbs to tell us which layer dropped the event. Today it just said "watcher inactive" or nothing at all. Not useful.

If you want to watch it live, the magic words are:

log stream --predicate 'subsystem == "com.ericwillis.avpainreliever" AND category == "config-watcher"' --level debug --style compact

The trace is .debug level which means it doesn't land in Save Logs for Support captures (those grab .notice and above only). So it doesn't bulk up your reports. Live diagnostic only.

Carry on.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.17-dev.5
item.description:
A polish pass, dev.5. Two fixes. Money.

Windows actually open centered now. Settings, About, Add Profile — they all used to flash through some random saved position before snapping to center, or sometimes just stay off-center on the wrong monitor. Done. Every time you open one, it lands centered on the screen your cursor is on. Move it, close it, reopen — centered again. Click another app, click back — not centered again (that'd be obnoxious). The polish you don't notice until it's there.

A weird "swiftpm-testing-helper added to your login items" notification that you may have seen. That was a self-inflicted wound from running the test suite. Test code was triggering a real macOS API that registers the current process as a login item — and under swift test the current process is the test runner. Every test run, another registration. macOS Sequoia finally got loud about it. Test code now uses a no-op stub for that path. If you saw the notification, pop into System Settings → Login Items & Extensions and remove swiftpm-testing-helper from "Open at Login" — fix prevents future registrations but doesn't undo the existing one. One-time cleanup.

Carry on.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.17
item.description:
Five dev releases of soak time, no bug reports, time to call it stable. Here's the headlines.

You can edit profiles from anywhere now. Used to be: you're sitting at home, you want to swap the Conference Room dock's mic from the Yeti to an AT2020, you couldn't, because the Yeti's not plugged in, it's not in the dropdown, stuck till Tuesday. Done. The wizard remembers every audio device and camera selection each profile has used. Open Edit on any profile from anywhere — its saved devices show up, marked "(not connected)" if they aren't, and you swap them right there. Per-profile, so the home dock's CalDigit doesn't leak into Conference Room's mic picker. That'd be amateur hour.

Hand-edit profiles.toml and it just works. No more "Reload Config" click in the Advanced menu. Save the file in any editor — VS Code, vim, TextEdit, doesn't matter — and within a quarter second the engine reloads. Audio defaults switch, camera switches, notification pops if the active profile changed. The "Re-evaluate Now" button is gone too. Two fewer rows in the Advanced submenu, same capabilities, less clicking.

A typo in profiles.toml no longer eats your config. Used to be: you save a broken TOML, the app silently overwrites it with the 1-profile starter, every custom profile gone. That was nuts. Now: broken copy gets renamed to profiles.corrupted-{timestamp}.toml right next to the active config. A notification pops with a Show in Finder button. Click it, your data's sitting right there, fix the typo, copy the section back. Money.

Windows actually open centered. Settings, About, Add Profile — they used to flash through some random position before snapping, or just stay off-center on the wrong monitor. Done. Center on every open, on the screen your cursor is on. Move it, close it, reopen — centered again. Click away to another app, click back — not centered again (that'd be obnoxious).

Plus polish: bigger confetti when you add a profile and it falls slower so you can actually see it. Sparkle's update-available window stops carrying extra chrome it doesn't need.

And a new release channel. There's a "dev" track now, separate from experimental. Opt in via Settings → General → Updates and you get small in-flight features as they ship, on a slightly faster cadence. Independent of the experimental moonshot track. Stay on stable, opt into one, opt into both — pick your pace.

That's the update. Five fixes worth of polish, plus a config file that won't betray you anymore. Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.18
item.description:
Couch problem? Solved. Plug your phone into your Mac to charge, plug a random USB stick in, do anything that creates a new device combination AV Pain Reliever hasn't seen before — it used to spot that, fire a "new location detected" toast, and put "Set Up Location…" in the menu. Asking you to capture the couch as a location. The couch is not a location. So now there's a "Not a Location" button right next to "Set Up Location…". One click, that exact device combination goes on the ignore list, the prompt never bothers you about it again. Money.

Want to undo it? Settings → Profiles → Ignored Locations shows every dismissal with the device names and a "Dismissed 12 minutes ago" timestamp. Trash button on any row pulls it out of the ignore list, and the next time those devices attach the prompt comes back. Changed your mind, that's allowed.

Couple of bugs got squashed in the same release:

  • "Set Up Location…" used to get stuck. Plug your phone in, unplug it, the menu still acted like you were at an unrecognized dock. The engine fired the enter unknown edge, the exit unknown edge wasn't wired. It is now. Devices go away, prompt goes away.
  • The menu label was middle-truncating as "Set Up...ocation…" on some displays because SwiftUI sized the NSMenu width before the conditional row appeared and never widened. Trimmed "This" out of the label, fits clean. Same item, same destination, no more stutter.

That's the deal. Couch protection, ghost-prompt slayed, truncation gone. Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.19
item.description:
Settings glow-up. The Profiles tab was the last screen in Settings still rendering with the plain-list look while General, Camera, and Stats had all moved to the rounded-card chrome that every modern Mac settings window uses. Felt out of place. Now it doesn't. Same buttons, same list, same edit and trash and add-profile affordances. New shell. Rounded cards, bold section headers, proper spacing, the works. Looks like it belongs in macOS. Money.

That's the whole release. Pure cosmetic. No new features, no settings to flip, no behavior changed. If you somehow loved the old plain-list look, our condolences.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.20
item.description:
What's new

Two quality-of-life fixes, both from the "stop bugging me" department.

Your flash drive is not a location. Plug in a USB stick, a card reader, your phone on a charge cable — the app used to see that and go "new location! let's set it up!" like an over-eager concierge. Done with that. It now checks what a device actually is before counting it as evidence you've moved desks. Drives and phones get politely ignored; docks, hubs, webcams, keyboards still count, because those are the things desks are made of. And when it genuinely can't tell what something is, it errs on the side of asking — missing your real new dock would be worse than one extra prompt. That's the deal.

Straight talk about restarts. When the virtual camera got wedged after an update, Settings used to tell you to restart the app — and sometimes that advice was flat-out wrong, because macOS was holding the old camera extension hostage until reboot, and no number of app restarts was going to spring it. Now the app asks macOS which situation you're actually in and tells you the truth: "Restart required" when relaunching the app fixes it, "Mac restart required" when only a reboot will do. No more clicking a button that can't possibly work. Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.21
item.description:
What's new

You know what's worse than no camera? A camera that says everything's fine and shows you a black rectangle. v0.2.0.21 fixes that. If your profile points the virtual camera at an HDMI capture card, the old build would open the card, report success, and then deliver exactly zero frames — because capture cards don't stream for anybody who won't name a format. So now we name it. Resolution, frame rate, in writing. The card wakes up, your video shows up, everyone's happy.

While we were in there, the recovery flow got a tune-up. When a leftover extension copy from an update blocks the camera, Settings used to jump straight to "restart your Mac." Turns out a ten-second toggle off-and-on usually does it — so that's the new first suggestion, and the full restart is the fallback, not the opener. The extension detector also learned some patience: macOS occasionally takes its sweet time spawning the camera extension, and we used to call it dead after 8 seconds. Now we give it a real chance, and we keep checking after that, quietly, just in case it shows up fashionably late.

One more, for the battery watchers: the camera engine now naps when nobody's watching and nothing's flowing. Fewer wakeups, less CPU, cooler laps. You won't see it — that's the point. Money.

item.title: Version 0.2.0.22-dev.1
item.description:
Two quality-of-life moves in this one, and they're both about trust.

First: Settings → Camera has a live preview now. A real one. It opens the virtual camera exactly the way Zoom opens it, so when that picture is moving, the whole pipeline is moving: extension, relay, frames, everything. Full width, mirrored like every self-view should be, with a status line that names the frame rate and the camera actually on the air. And it's honest: if you're looking at a held frame instead of live video, it says so instead of flashing a green dot at you.

Second: you know the move where the camera goes invisible after an update and the answer was "restart the app"? The app knows the move too. Now it notices when macOS has frozen its view of the camera, posts a heads-up, restarts itself once, and comes back seeing clearly. Once. Never a loop. And if a restart wouldn't actually fix your situation, it skips the theater and gives you the advice that will.

Money.
